title: Review the 23 SECURITY DEFINER functions the public (anon) role can call, starting with the guest-RSVP, signup-lead and guest-seat ones

source.ref: Whole-site audit 2026-11-16 (project thread, requested by Daniel). Confidence: CONFIRMED. Audit file: audit/FINAL-BUILD-AND-REPAIR-LIST-2026-11-16.md

detail:
EVIDENCE: Supabase security advisor, Frequency Community, 2026-11-16: anon_security_definer_function_executable 23, authenticated 56. Most are intended public readers (public_events, public_circles, public_posts, public_member_count). The write-capable ones are capture_guest_rsvp, capture_signup_lead, update_signup_lead, read_guest_seat, update_guest_seat, release_guest_seat, handle_is_available.

WHY IT MATTERS: A definer function callable by anyone runs with owner rights. The write ones must prove their own authorization (token, rate, ownership) inside the function; nothing in the repo records that review.

FIX DIRECTION: Write docs/security/definer-rpc-review.md: for each anon-callable function, what it can read or write and what checks it makes; revoke execute from anon where the app does not need it.

2026-11-16 fixed (security thread): review written in docs/security/definer-rpc-review.md from read-only SQL on production (no migration applied). Authorization checks hold on all 7 write-capable functions; no revoke applied because the app calls each through the anon cookie client. Real findings filed as SCAN-1245 (capture_guest_rsvp has no DB-side limit, P2) and SCAN-1246 (capture_signup_lead rotates claim tokens, P3).

verify.note: Fails on 2026-11-16 (audit run). Passes when the fix lands. Audit-written probes are direction checks; retime only with Daniel's phrase.
